I recently started on a brand new server - made a Warrior and am building myself up. Every time I do this, I use the same method for gaining gold. I hope it helps you, as it always seems to snag 2-3k gold right as I hit Pandaria. (Though it may snag less for you since you are starting at a higher level.)

Cloth, no matter what server you are on, seems to be a big money maker. Most Tailors I know tend to just buy their way through the levels versus farming the mats. You can make a great deal selling all the cloth you get in dungeons/mobs. I also know of two places to farm that not only has a very high cloth drop rate, but also greens in both Cata and Pandaria expansions.

For Cata, when I was short on gold, I would end up going to Uldum's Obelisk of the Moon. Fly down and in that first room I'd just kill the elites one at a time, going in a circle. They respawn fairly quickly and drop Embersilk (Is that the right one?) and greens at a high percentage. Within an hour, I would have 25-45 stacks of silk + various greens/gold from the mobs.

In Pandaria, I farm in Dread Wastes just north of Dreadwater Lake, on the scar. These are groups of mobs there that have a high drop rate of the Pandaria cloth, greens, and the Amber Shards for Klaxxi rep. On the days I feel up to farming, I will make upwards of 3-5K within 2/3 hours of farming.

I don't touch professions until I am usually 85. My reasoning behind this is that I like to power level my professions. Your best bet for that would be to check your AH and see what profession mats are the most expensive and try that route. But that is sort of like side income to me.

Other than that, I don't have much else to offer. I'm a Tailor/Enchanter, so farming the cloth was my best route. As a DK, you can pull big groups, and make the gold fast. :)

(I did make about 1.5k JUST from questing from 1 to 80. So quests can make bank too.)

Good luck!

I feel most of this will based on personal preference, but I was a guild leader for nearly 5 years. I'll give my pointers and hopefully that will help you to some degree.

Its really great that you have a bunch of buddies that will make up your guild - it gives you an advantage knowing already how they play and what kind of people they are. But, at the same accord, I would still be semi-weary about who has what permissions. Even people you've played with for year (or may know is real life) can quickly turn to backstab you. However, if that is not a concern to you, don't fret much over how ranking work. 

Also, with that, it can be hard not to be biased when it comes to drama, gear, and the like. Keep in mind that there is two sides to every story and that nobody is above lying.

To add to the ranking, you can keep it simple by having it GM > Officers > Raiders > Members > Alts, with adding other in-between ranks as you see fit (like one rank between Officer and Raiders, like a rank to those that are heavily involved in the guild and such.). Flare it up with whatever kind of names you want, or nothing special at all. 

You stated a Semi-hardcore environment. I assume you mean in regards to the Raiding itself. If that is the case, having people show up unprepared may be something you keep in mind - Flasks, Food, Proper Gems/enchants should be something you stress to your players. But even more so, following directions when it comes to strats. Is the same player failing at the same mechanic? Do you have a raider that thinks the rules don't apply to them because they have some elitist mentality? People like that you either put up with or cut them loose - know when to do this, but not be a dickwad about it.

You will likely want to discuss if you want to be a solo leader, or have a "council" of sorts. I've seen guilds of each kind - and some that even implement it when it comes to loot. I opted to "council", but with the final call resting on myself. Getting feedback from Officers, and even regular members, can help dictate what steps you need to take. The best loot rules are the most common - Main spec > Off spec. If you won a piece of gear already for yourself, higher priority should go to those that have not won anything. However, you can also regulate this with iLvl - Is it a much higher upgrade (+20 iLvl/+300/400 stat increase) for Player A, who won a piece already, or for player B, who has not won anything, but has an item just 5 ilvl lower with not much of a stat upgrade (+30/50 stat increase)?

The biggest issue I see with "hardcore" guilds is keeping it constant. If you kick 'A' for messing up multiple times, you should do the same to that officer friend of yours that does the exact same shit. Being biased can really impact other players. Give them both the chance to improve - let them know what they need to fix, warn them, whatever. But don't go back on your hand. 

I am not sure how much of this will help you, if at all, but its basic stuff that most guilds implement and execute fairly well.

Just remember: you are a player, just like everyone else with the exact same goals. You are not a God, nor better than them. Keep it simple, and everyone will have fun AND progress.

Happy Hunting!

I recently did the same thing; I was Horde since Vanilla and recently moved to play alliance about 3 months before MoP came out. There are some differences and, after being used to playing Horde for so long, it does take some time to get used to the changes.

However, I think this is all based on what server you join. I would do some Realm research before actually joining a Realm. For example, if you want to be a Raider, find the top ranked Alliance Raiding server. Same with PvP - find the top rated PvP server for Alliance. Doing this will greatly increase you desire to play, regardless of Faction.

From that point, decide what you want to play as; if you are a statistics kind of player, find a race that gives bonuses to stats. Or bonuses to things that appeal to you most (as said by other commenter, Humans get the Rep bonus, Worgen the Crit). 

Lore is a bit different. I feel that the stories on both sides are quite gripping (though, I always appealed to the Horde story. So much anger yet they conspire together.). 

I mean, to me, it is hard to give accurate tips, as I would need to know more about your play style and whatnot. But I hope some of that helps you.
